title: LitLinker: Supporting the Ideation of Interdisciplinary Contexts with Large Language Models for Teaching Literature in Elementary Schools
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’25)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge elementary school literature teachers face when designing interdisciplinary teaching contexts that connect reading materials with other subjects such as science, art, history, and music. The authors argue that teachers often use a “reverse thinking” process: they start from a promising interdisciplinary context and then search for texts that fit, but this requires substantial time, domain exploration, and judgment about whether the connections are educationally meaningful.

To support this workflow, the paper introduces LitLinker, a large language model-powered interactive system for elementary Chinese language teachers. LitLinker uses multiple LLM agent roles—Context Analyst, Text Analyst, Text Reviewer, and Context Summarizer—to recommend interdisciplinary contexts, analyze relationships between contexts and texts, support questions and edits, and generate structured lesson plans with introductions and classroom activities. The system is grounded in a context pool built from textbooks and educational materials, and its prompts are designed around teacher-derived evaluation criteria.

The paper reports two kinds of empirical evidence. First, a within-subjects study with 16 novice users of literature teaching compared LitLinker against a baseline LLM web application and found that LitLinker produced deeper integration of subjects, lower workload, and higher satisfaction and efficiency. Second, expert interviews with elementary Chinese language teachers supported the usefulness of the system and informed design principles for LLM-based teaching tools. Overall, the paper concludes that LLMs can support teacher ideation more effectively when they are embedded in structured, interactive workflows that match teachers’ practices rather than used as simple chat interfaces.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed CHI paper with a within-subjects comparison and expert interviews, but it is not an RCT in a classroom setting and the main users were novice teacher participants rather than authentic K-12 classroom implementation. The evidence is therefore qualitative/experimental HCI evidence with some concerns about ecological validity for the target setting.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows promising but modest evidence that the tool improves lesson-planning quality and reduces workload, yet it does not report effect sizes in the provided text and does not evaluate student learning outcomes. The impact is therefore suggestive rather than clearly demonstrated at a medium/large level.

interventions.use_case: LLM-powered teacher-facing system (LitLinker) for ideating interdisciplinary contexts, analyzing reading materials, answering teacher questions, and generating lesson plans for elementary literature instruction; compared against a plain LLM web app baseline.

finding.finding_summary: LitLinker improved the quality of interdisciplinary lesson-plan outputs for elementary Chinese literature teaching relative to a baseline LLM web app. The paper reports that the generated plans had deeper integration of different subjects and were judged against literacy-oriented criteria such as content alignment and educational-objective alignment, but does not provide a numeric effect size in the text excerpt provided.
finding.measure: Expert-rated quality of lesson plans for Chinese literature instruction, including content alignment, alignment with educational objectives, and depth of integration

finding.finding_summary: LitLinker reduced teachers’ workload and was judged more efficient than the baseline LLM web app during interdisciplinary lesson planning. The abstract and study description state that it significantly reduced task workload and increased satisfaction/efficiency, but no numeric effect sizes are reported in the excerpt provided.
finding.measure: NASA-TLX workload ratings; perceived efficiency and satisfaction (SUS-adapted items)
